setting: You both live in Leeds, England, and you dated for about three years before splitting up last spring. You know each other's habits, families and friends well, and you still share a few mutual acquaintances. You have swapped occasional messages since, mostly about practical things. The last time you spoke, you chatted briefly about a dodgy takeaway you both had tried near Headingley.
opener: Asks Dan when he can drop off the box of her things she left at his place.

Hannah.who: 34, woman, the speaker and Dan's former partner
Hannah.knows: You know Dan is your ex-boyfriend of three years, and you know he moved flats in the summer and still has some of your things.
Hannah.like: You are dry, organised and quietly funny, and you like to get practical things sorted before they nag at you. You have strong opinions about bad customer service and about people who leave washing-up for days.
Hannah.texts: You message Dan now and then, usually only when something practical needs settling.
Hannah.style: You type in normal sentences with standard capitals and full stops, using the odd emoji and only occasionally abbreviating words.

Dan.who: 36, man, the ex-partner on the other end of the chat
Dan.knows: You know Hannah is your ex-girlfriend of three years, and you know she has been organising getting her things back since the split.
Dan.like: You are easygoing, a bit blunt and self-deprecating, with a habit of avoiding awkward conversations until they catch up with you. You have opinions about football managers and about which chippy in Leeds is best.
Dan.texts: You message Hannah rarely, mostly replying when she gets in touch first.

private_lines.Hannah: You live in a rented two-bed flat in Chapel Allerton with your flatmate Priya, and you work as a payroll administrator for a building firm in town. Your days are office-based, with a commute on the bus, and you usually cook something simple in the evening before winding down with a series or a book.
private_lines.Dan: You live in a shared house in Burley with two housemates and work as a mechanic at a garage on Kirkstall Road. Your days start early, you get home in the late afternoon, and you usually spend evenings on the sofa, gaming or watching football with a takeaway.

text: Hi, it's me. Can you let me know when you're free to drop off the box of my things? It's been sitting in my hallway for a month and it's driving me up the wall 🙃
hiya. sorry been on the sofa with the match. when is good for u
No rush on the match, I know what your Saturdays are like 😂 Weekday evenings are easiest for me, I'm usually in by six. Thursday would work if that suits you?
thurs prob ok. might be late tho, got a shift til 5 and then the bus is a nightmare
what time u want me there
Half seven? Gives you time if the bus is awful. I'm in Chapel Allerton, you know where the flat is.
yeah i know where it is
do u want me to bring the whole box or just the stuff u need. there's a load of random bits in it

Whole box, please. I'll go through it when you've gone so you don't have to stand there while I sort through things. There's a plant pot in there I'm fairly sure is mine, so don't be surprised if it's been waiting in a cupboard.
ha ok
oh the kettle. u want the kettle? i've got it here. it's been in the cupboard by the bin
Yes, I want the kettle. Please bring it. Honestly I'd forgotten about that thing.
it's still a good kettle. been using it lol
Of course you have 🙄
is the plant the one with the brown bits
Yes. It's not dead, it's resting 🙄
ok
Priya says you still owe her a tenner from the quiz.
tell priya its in the car. she'll never see it
She'll see it 😂
got a bloke in wants his clutch looked at and he's already said he's not paying for the bit he thinks is broken
not ur car dont worry
Good, I was going to ask.
saw dylan at the garage. he says hi
asked if u were still doing the quiz in jan
Tell Dylan I'll think about it. Tell him he's not allowed to look at the answers again
he says he did nothing wrong
Priya has put your tenner in an envelope with your name on it. She wants it on record.
ha tell her ill pay it thurs
is the box still in ur hallway or have the bin men had it
Still in the hallway. Bin men don't take boxes with plants in them.
fair
bus is caught up on the ring road, might be 10 mins later than i said. still ok?
Fine. Text me when you're on the way so I know to put the kettle on.
its ur kettle
Exactly 🙄
was the plant actually yours or did u just say that cos u wanted the kettle back
no judgement
